Corroborated by plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md, section 'Design notes only (no build)' and its 2026-09-06 'Design notes' execution record: "MLA tuples (576/512, 320/256): the same k-chunked structure covers asymmetric (qk, v) by chunking the K axis independently of the V axis (llama.cpp proves the pattern on Turing); rope-split dims ride the same loop. Design note, not a commitment." Item recorded in research/lacunae/outline.yaml (category: kernels). The fork's vLLM lane carries the object under study: software/vllm/main/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/triton_mla.py (lane at v0.28.1rc0-23, file last touched 2026-08-21 by #51718).
current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the MLA serving surface is split into a Hopper/Blackwell fast path and a portable Triton fallback, and the tuple space this item targets is now shipped model space, not theory. (1) FlashMLA (deepseek-ai/FlashMLA): support matrix is SM90/SM100 only - dense decode SM90 (MQA, BF16 KV), sparse decode SM90+SM100 (FP8 KV), dense prefill SM100 (MHA), sparse prefill SM90+SM100; CUDA 12.8+ (12.9+ for SM100); MQA mode is exactly the 576/512 tuple (head_dim_k=576, head_dim_v=512). Timeline: public Feb 2025 (Hopper-only, 'H800 SXM5'); 2025-04-22 perf update (up to 3000 GB/s memory-bound, 660 TFLOPS compute-bound on H800); 2025-08-01 SM100 MHA prefill via NVIDIA PR; 2025-09-29 sparse (DSA) kernels with DeepSeek-V3.2 (FP8 KV 656 B/token = 512 B NoPE e4m3 + 16 B scales + 128 B unquantized bf16 RoPE; 410 TFLOPS sparse decode on H800, ~350 on B200). (2) vLLM (fork lane v0.28.1rc0-era, Aug 2026): the docs 'Attention Backend Feature Support' matrix lists MLA decode backends FLASHMLA (9.x-10.x), FLASH_ATTN_MLA (9.x), CUTLASS_MLA/FLASHINFER_MLA/TOKENSPEED_MLA (10.x), FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (9.x) / _SM120 (12.x), and TRITON_MLA with Compute Cap 'Any', KV dtypes auto/float16/bfloat16/fp8/fp8_e4m3, block sizes %16, head sizes Any, DCP yes. Source confirms supports_compute_capability() returns True unconditionally; the only pre-Hopper-aware code is in TritonMLAImpl.__init__ (triton_mla.py:199-223): FP8 KV rejected below SM89 ('native FP8 (fp8e4nv) requires SM89+'), bfloat16 KV rejected below SM80, with the error explicitly suggesting --kv-cache-dtype float16 for cap < 80 - i.e. the float16-KV sm75 configuration is a code-anticipated path, but no public run of TRITON_MLA on sm75 exists [uncertain]. The kernel is vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_decode_attention.py (AMD-originated, HIP branches): split-KV decode with fp32 LSE merge, BLOCK_H=16, num_stages 1-2, handles D_QK=576/BLOCK_DMODEL=512 and in-kernel fp8->bf16 dequant (Mode 1); VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT forces num_kv_splits=1 for deterministic reduction. Introduced by vLLM PRs #12528 (2025-01-31, MLA decode optimizations), #12601 (2025-02-01, DeepSeek V3 MLA FP8 compute), #12639 (2025-02-21, chunked prefill). Real-world Ampere datapoint (croz.net, DeepSeek V3-0324 heavy-load benchmark, 2025): 'On A100 GPUs vLLM can use TritonMLA only which shows limited performance during decoding compared to FlashMLA.' No Triton MLA prefill backend exists for CUDA in the lane (prefill backends: FLASH_ATTN listed 'Any' CC, TRTLLM_RAGGED/FLASHINFER/TOKENSPEED_MLA SM100-only). (3) Sparse MLA (DSA) non-Hopper gap: vLLM #38006 (2026-03-24, open, PR #38476 linked) requests TRITON_MLA_SPARSE for sm80/sm120/121 - 'GLM-5 and other models using DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) cannot run on sm80 GPUs (A100/A800)'; three blocker layers named (dsv3_fused_a_gemm unconditionally compiles sm90+ code; no sparse MLA backend below sm90; sparse_attn_indexer calls DeepGemm fp8_mqa_logits without an is_deep_gemm_supported() guard); a PoC (triton_mla_sparse.py + triton_sparse_decode_attention.py + fp8_mqa_logits_fallback.py) ran GLM-5-FP8 (744B) correctly on 8xA800 with 40GB cpu_offload, no throughput numbers. vLLM #30644 tracks the missing auto-fallback for FLASHMLA_SPARSE (SM90/SM100 only); a HF discussion on QuantTrio/DeepSeek-V3.2-AWQ confirms V3.2 sparse attention does not run on Ampere. (4) DeepSeek V4 (2026): the lane carries vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py with FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4 / FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 / ROCM variants sharing the 'V4 sparse-index pipeline (compressor + SWA + indexer, 256-token blocks, head 512)'; docs list FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 at 10.x/12.x and FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4 at 'Any' (registry entry exists but the underlying FlashMLA kernels are SM90/SM100 - the 'Any' row is a doc-level claim [uncertain]); Triton metadata kernels (c128a topk builder, sparse_mla_triton_warmup.py) are already part of the DSV4 path. (5) Model side of the tuples: 576/512 = kv_lora_rank 512 + rope 64 (DeepSeek V2/V3/R1/V3.2, Kimi-K2-class, GLM-4.7-Flash per the TurboQuant llama.cpp fork whose v1.4.1 added 'Full TurboQuant support for MLA architecture models: GLM-4.7-Flash, DeepSeek-V2/V3' with 'asymmetric K=concat(latent[512], rope[64])=576 dims and V=latent[512]'); 320/256 = kv_lora_rank 256 + rope 64 - Mistral Small 4 119B (released 2026-03-16, config kv_lora_rank=256, qk_nope_head_dim=64, qk_rope_head_dim=64, 1M context, MoE 128 experts). GLM-5 (2026, arXiv:2602.15763) is MLA+DSA at 744B; GLM-5.3-Flash is a hybrid KDA + sparse-MLA 320B/18B MoE. (6) Vendor-neutral implementations: llama.cpp merged MLA via PR #12801 (May 2025) with the combined 576-dim K-only cache (V derived from K; ~47% KV-cache saving; Q8_0 K cache enables 128K-160K+ contexts on 24GB-class cards); its ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_turing table instantiates exactly (320,256) and (576,512) for sm_75. ik_llama.cpp ships FlashMLA-2 (ikawrakow's own fattn-mma-family kernel, not DeepSeek's SM90 library) with Q8_0 KV on CUDA since 2025-03-12 ('Allow Q8_0 KV cache with FlashMLA-2 on CUDA'; 2025-03-10 new 8-bit KV type) and FlashMLA-3 (best on CPU; CUDA Ampere+ per its docs); ik_llama common.cuh defines INT8_MMA_AVAILABLE for __CUDA_ARCH__ >= CC_TURING (750) with CP_ASYNC_AVAILABLE gated to Ampere, i.e. the mma MLA path is compiled for sm_75 with single-stage loads; its discussion #354 (2025-04-29, RTX 4080, DeepSeek-Lite Q4_0) shows 1.8x-2.5x CUDA PP and 1.8x TG vs mainline MLA with 2.15x less cache memory (972 MiB K-only vs 1836 MiB KV at 32k). llama.cpp's generic DSA implementation merged as PR #23346 (release b9411, 2026) after fairydreaming's #21149 + testing discussion #21183 (opened 2026-03-30; CUDA works on 12.x after rebase; tested on 8x RTX PRO 6000S; 'DSA attention works exactly like MLA up to 2048 tokens').
sm75_viability: Measured MLA numbers on Turing-class hardware: none exist anywhere upstream - TRITON_MLA has no public sm75 run [uncertain], FlashMLA cannot compile for sm75 (SM90/SM100 only), and every CUDA/Blackwell MLA backend in vLLM's matrix (CUTLASS_MLA, FLASHINFER_MLA, TOKENSPEED_MLA, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_*) is 10.x-gated. What the evidence says CAN run on sm_75: (a) vLLM TRITON_MLA decode, nominally - supports_compute_capability() is unconditionally True, the fp16-KV variant is the code-anticipated pre-sm80 configuration (fp8 KV hard-fails below SM89, bf16 KV below SM80, error text suggests float16), and the kernel has no arch-conditional Triton code - but on this host it rides the Triton codegen floor: the lane pins triton <=3.2 (Triton dropped Volta/Turing in 3.3 per triton #5066), and tl.dot lowers to Volta mma.884 at half Turing-native mma.1688 throughput (triton #189) or to scalar/FMA when shapes do not match - so the emulated path is compute-crippled for prefill-shaped work and only bandwidth-bound decode (b small) escapes the math ceiling; MLA absorbed decode is MQA-shaped (1 KV head, q heads x 576/512), which is the friendliest possible case for split-KV bandwidth-bound Triton decode. It is also decode-only: no Triton MLA prefill kernel exists for CUDA in vLLM, and the FA2-class prefill path is gate-0 disqualified on sm75 by plan/0007's own probes (FA2 sub-sm80 d=128 silently wrong max_err 2.20; d=256 launch failure cudaErrorInvalidValue). (b) The CUDA-native precedent that proves the tuples on sm75 today: llama.cpp fattn-mma (INT8_MMA_AVAILABLE >= CC_TURING; single-stage loads, no cp.async below sm_80) ships turing config-table entries for exactly (320,256) and (576,512) - the absorbed-MLA shapes of Mistral Small 4 and DeepSeek/GLM-4.7-Flash - and ik_llama's FlashMLA-2 rides the same macros with Q8_0 K-cache on top; measured only on Ada (RTX 4080) publicly, sm75 execution is compile-gate-supported but not benchmark-reported [uncertain]. (c) The fork's own bridge kernel: plan/0007's k-chunked structure extends to the MLA tuples by chunking the K axis independently of the V axis (576 K -> 576 = 4.5x128 chains against 512 V = 4x128, rope-split dims in the same loop), at full mma.1688-class tensor-core rate (the d=256 template already sustains 22.0-24.3 TFLOP/s fp32-accumulated on this card). Attention-backend candidate matrix for absorbed MLA decode (576/512) on sm_75: FLASHMLA no (SM90/SM100), FLASHINFER_MLA/CUTLASS_MLA/TOKENSPEED_MLA no (SM100), FLASH_ATTN_MLA no (SM90 + FA2 sub-sm80 gate-0 disqualified), TRITON_MLA conditionally (any-CC code, fp16 KV only, mma.884/FMA math floor, unmeasured), ROCM_AITER n/a (AMD), BRIDGE_ATTN yes after the 576/512+320/256 instantiations land (design-note status). Fallback semantics: KV dtype must be float16 on sm75 (fp8 and bf16 both rejected by explicit ValueError, not silent fallback) and the MLA absorption means a K-only 576-dim cache (53% of the naive 2x576 fp16 KV; Q8_0 K halves it again per the llama.cpp/ik_llama pattern, untested for numerics on this host). DSA on sm75: no vLLM path below sm90 exists or is merged (#38006 open since 2026-03-24); llama.cpp's generic DSA (#23346) is the only vendor-neutral implementation and is arch-generic CUDA, but is untested on sm75 and still under lineage-bench validation; below 2048 tokens DSA degenerates to exactly dense MLA, so a dense-MLA sm75 path is the first 100% of the DSA surface.

effort_estimate: Stage 12 as written is a registry row + measurement, and that is the right size for the first slice: wire TRITON_MLA into the fork's attention selection for an MLA model config (float16 KV forced - the pre-sm80 branch of the existing ValueError already defines the contract), extend the fp64 oracle with absorbed-MLA cases (576/512 and 320/256, MQA decode with rope-split handling, chunked prefix), gate-0 it against torch references, then measure decode tok/s on the two cards. Realistic size: days, dominated by the MLA metadata/paged-cache plumbing (block_size %16) rather than the kernel itself. The second slice - the bridge instantiation of the same tuples (K-axis and V-axis chunked independently, per the plan/0007 design note) - is a kernel-ladder entry comparable to but smaller than the d512 item (576/512 and 320/256 fit the existing smem class at 32-row KV tiles since K and V tiles are chunked, not doubled), sized at roughly the plan/0007 d=256 step x 1.5. A third slice (Q8_0 K-cache on the bridge MLA path, the ik_llama/llama.cpp memory lever) is an optional strategy row. Out of scope for stage 12 and correctly so: DSA sparse attention below sm90 is a full campaign (indexer + top-k + gather attention; vLLM has not even merged its sm80 version, #38006 open).
unlocks: Execution of the MLA model class on sm_75 with attested numerics: DeepSeek-V2-Lite/V3-family and GLM-4.7-Flash (576/512) and Mistral Small 4 119B (320/256) - the KV-footprint economics are the operator-relevant part (MLA latent cache is ~53% of naive fp16 KV at q-heavy head counts and, with the Q8_0 K pattern, ~27%; on 2x24 GB this is what makes any long-context MLA model plausible at all). Secondarily it unblocks the DSA family's first 2048 tokens everywhere (DSA == dense MLA below 2048 per llama.cpp discussion #21183), so a validated dense-MLA sm75 path is the substrate any future non-Hopper DSA emulation lands on; it also retires the last head-shape class (asymmetric qk/v) the bridge kernel has no answer for, completing the attention coverage table for dense models.
dependency_order: Must land first: plan/0005 stage 11 (the Turing-capable engine itself - every other row is unreachable on current upstream without it; already the fork's retained surface) and the fp64-oracle extension for asymmetric (qk,v) tuples before any timing (gate-0 discipline; oracle harness exists, extends by case-adding). No new external prerequisites: triton <=3.2 is already pinned in the lane; the TRITON_MLA backend is already in the lane tree; CUDA 13.3 toolchain in place. Parallelizable from day one: (a) the TRITON_MLA measurement slice (pure engine/registry work), (b) the bridge-kernel 576/512+320/256 instantiation (pure kernel work, oracle shared), (c) llama.cpp/ik_llama fattn-mma builds on this card as the independent adjudication witnesses (their turing tables ship exactly these shapes). Sequencing inside the bridge slice: oracle cases -> template with independent K/V chunking -> ptxas zero-spill assert -> shim/scope/tests -> bench. The Q8_0-K strategy row must follow the fp16-K numerics attestation, never precede it.
risk_notes: Correctness/numerics: (1) absorbed-MLA decode changes the numerics profile - the rope-split sub-block (64 of 576) rides the same softmax as the latent block, and fp16 K-storage of the 576-dim combined key has different saturation behavior than per-head fp16 (the TurboQuant fork measured rope norm ~10.49 vs latent ~0.13, a 80x magnitude spread inside one dot product - the fp64 oracle must include magnitude-regression cases for exactly this); (2) silently-wrong is the dominant hazard on this host (plan/0007 gate-0 disqualifications of FA2 sub-sm80 and FlashInfer prefill) - TRITON_MLA 'runs' on any CC by code inspection but has literally never been validated on sm75 anywhere, so its first run is a correctness experiment, not a benchmark; (3) Q8_0 K-cache (the ik_llama lever) is a quality-changing quantization - it must be measured against fp16-K output quality, not just attested for faithful value-storage. Upstream-drift exposure: high on the TRITON_MLA path - the MLA backend matrix churned repeatedly in 2025-2026 (DCP, batch-invariance mode, DSpark non-causal, KV-cache layout refactor #51718 on 2026-08-21, DSV4 sparse family), and #38006's TRITON_MLA_SPARSE (sm80 floor) may land and re-shape the non-Hopper story mid-campaign; low on the bridge-kernel path (no upstream sm75 CUDA MLA exists to drift against). Performance honesty: the emulated path is expected slow (mma.884/FMA math floor; croz.net measured TritonMLA 'limited performance during decoding compared to FlashMLA' even on A100), and the contract is execution-with-attested-numerics, so a slow number is a deliverable, not a failure.
determinism_class: Two mechanisms with different classes. TRITON_MLA decode: statistical, not bitwise - split-KV decomposition with fp32 LSE merge means the reduction order depends on num_kv_splits (computed from SM count and max_seq_len, so config- and occupancy-dependent); vLLM's own VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT mode exists precisely because of this and forces num_kv_splits=1 for deterministic reduction - the fork's gate should pin batch-invariant mode (or pin the split count) for oracle runs and record run-to-run spread otherwise; no atomics are involved, so restart-to-restart variance is scheduling-level, not order-level. Bridge-kernel MLA instantiation: bitwise deterministic for a fixed launch configuration (no atomics, no split-K, compile-time chunk order), same class as the delivered d=64/128/256 kernels; the independent K/V chunking changes the fp32 partial-sum boundaries vs the symmetric case, so its error envelope vs the fp64 oracle must be re-measured, not inherited. Gate discipline: correctness asserts single-run (kernel bitwise stable; TRITON_MLA after split-pinning), performance judged on median-of-N with the cross-restart methodology plan/0007 fixed (tp2 arms medianed across at least three engine restarts).
priority_signal: For: the tuples stopped being hypothetical in 2026 - Mistral Small 4 (2026-03-16) made 320/256 shipping model space and GLM-4.7-Flash/DeepSeek keep 576/512 the default; MLA is the KV-footprint lever that matters most on 2x24 GB; the TRITON_MLA backend already contains the pre-sm80 float16-KV branch (the upstream authors at least contemplated the configuration); the CUDA-native precedents (llama.cpp turing table, ik_llama FlashMLA-2 + Q8_0) prove the shapes run on sm75 silicon today; and the bridge alternative rides a landed, gate-tested kernel family, so the marginal cost is a template instantiation, not a research program. Against: the emulated path is decode-only (no Triton MLA prefill exists upstream) and compute-crippled on sm75's Triton floor, so TRITON_MLA alone cannot serve an MLA model end-to-end on this host - prefill still needs the bridge kernel, which makes the bridge instantiation the real deliverable and TRITON_MLA merely the cheap first measurement and the independent cross-check; the full-size MLA models (DeepSeek 671B, GLM-5 744B, Mistral 119B bf16) do not fit 2x24 GB except heavily quantized or partial, so operator value concentrates in the small/quant MLA tier (DeepSeek-V2-Lite class, GLM-4.7-Flash class, Q4-ish Mistral Small 4) [uncertain: which concrete checkpoints the operator would actually run]; and the window has no urgency - nothing upstream is moving toward sm75 (the one relevant upstream motion, #38006, targets sm80+, not sm75), so deferral costs nothing but delays the only Turing MLA path that will ever exist. Net: medium priority - do the cheap TRITON_MLA gate-0 measurement now for the record, and land the bridge 576/512+320/256 instantiation when an MLA checkpoint actually enters the serving mix.
recommended_probe: Gate-0 probe, no timing until numerics are proven, one evening of card time: (1) instantiate an MLA-scaled test object in the fork lane - synthetic absorbed-MQA weights at 576/512 and 320/256 (1 KV head, rope-split 64), or DeepSeek-V2-Lite if a GGUF/safetensors checkpoint is at hand; (2) force TRITON_MLA with kv-cache-dtype float16 (the pre-sm80 branch of triton_mla.py's own ValueError), pin VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (num_kv_splits=1) so the oracle comparison is order-stable, and differential-check decode output against a torch fp32/fp64 absorbed-MLA reference AND a second witness - either the plan/0007 oracle extended with the asymmetric tuples or llama.cpp fattn-mma built for sm75 (its turing table ships exactly 320/256 and 576/512), with magnitude-regression cases targeting the rope(10.49)-vs-latent(0.13) spread; (3) record the verdict per gate 0: silently-wrong = disqualified + blocker note, correct = proceed to decode tok/s at kv=1024/4096/16384, median-of-3, same protocol as the FlashInfer d=256 baseline rows. Success criterion: oracle ALL PASS at both tuples with max_err profile comparable to the d=64/128/256 family; performance is recorded whatever it is (slow-but-correct is the deliverable; the bridge instantiation decision is then a per-FLOP comparison, not a viability question).
